I'm working on the HTTP transport layer for a Google Cloud client library.

*   The otelAttributeTransport struct must have a logger field of type *slog.Logger so that a structured logger can be attached when constructing the transport directly.

*   A concrete type named errorTrackingBody must be defined in the httptransport package. It must implement io.ReadCloser so it can replace an http.Response.Body. Callers must be able to perform a *errorTrackingBody type assertion on the response body.

*   When the experimental logging feature flag (GOOGLE_SDK_GO_EXPERIMENTAL_LOGGING) is enabled and an HTTP response indicates an error, the transport must emit exactly one DEBUG-level structured JSON log record per request/response cycle.

*   The log record for an HTTP error response must include the following fields: msg (the error message string from the response body), rpc.system.name set to 'http', rpc.response.status_code (gRPC-style status string), http.response.status_code (numeric HTTP status code as a number), http.request.method, and error.type.

*   If the response body contains a google.rpc.ErrorInfo detail entry with a recognized actionable reason (such as RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED or IAM_PERMISSION_DENIED), error.type must be set to that reason string. If multiple ErrorInfo entries are present, the first one with an actionable reason must be used.

*   If the ErrorInfo entry includes a domain field, the log record must include gcp.errors.domain set to that domain. If the ErrorInfo entry includes a metadata map, each key-value pair must appear in the log record as gcp.errors.metadata.<key>.

*   If the request context carries a telemetry value for 'resend_count', the log record must include http.request.resend_count as a number. If the context carries 'resource_name', the log record must include gcp.resource.destination.id.

*   For a context.DeadlineExceeded transport error, the log record must set error.type to 'CLIENT_TIMEOUT' and rpc.response.status_code to 'DEADLINE_EXCEEDED'. For context.Canceled, error.type must be 'CLIENT_CANCELLED' and rpc.response.status_code must be 'CANCELED'. For any other error without an HTTP response, error.type must be the Go reflect type name of the error (e.g. '*errors.errorString') and rpc.response.status_code must be 'UNKNOWN'.

*   When the experimental logging feature flag is disabled, the transport must produce no log output whatsoever; the round trip must complete without any logging side effects.

*   The log record must NOT be emitted until the response body is closed. When the log is emitted on body close, any active OpenTelemetry span associated with the request must still be recording at that moment.

*   When a response body's ContentLength is greater than 8192 (8 KB), the transport must log immediately using the HTTP status string (e.g. '400 Bad Request') as the message, and must NOT wrap the body in an errorTrackingBody wrapper.

*   When a response body's actual content exceeds 8192 bytes (but ContentLength is unknown), the transport must fall back to the HTTP status string as the log message.

*   When the response body is closed before being fully read (early close), or when reading the body produces a network error, the transport must still emit a log record.

*   Logging and tracing must operate independently. Enabling only tracing must add telemetry span attributes (such as gcp.client.version) to spans but emit no log records. Enabling only logging must emit log records for error responses but must not add the telemetry attributes to spans. Enabling both must do both. Disabling both must do neither (though a span is still created).

## httptransport Package Overview

The Package httptransport provides functionality for managing HTTP client connections to Google Cloud services. Its key functions include AddAuthorizationMiddleware, which adds a middleware to the provided client's transport that sets the Authorization header with the value produced by the provided credentials, and NewClient, which returns a net/http.Client that can be used to communicate with a Google cloud service. It automatically appends Authorization headers to all outgoing requests.

## Logging with slog

The package uses Go's standard `log/slog` for debug logging. Across the auth options structures, the `Logger` field is defined consistently: Logger is used for debug logging. If provided, logging will be enabled at the logger's configured level. By default logging is disabled unless enabled by setting GOOGLE_SDK_GO_LOGGING_LEVEL in which case a default logger will be used. Optional. Logger *slog.Logger.

## Summary

I implemented the experimental structured-error-logging feature for the HTTP transport layer. Since the gRPC transport (`grpctransport/grpctransport.go`) already had the parallel feature, I modeled the HTTP implementation on it while adapting to HTTP's specifics (the error details live in the response body rather than in a Go error/`stats.End`).

**Files changed (source only — no `tests/` touched):**

- **`auth/httptransport/httptransport_otel.go`** (new) — moved the OTel transport here and added logging:
  - `otelAttributeTransport` now has a `logger *slog.Logger` field (constructible directly, as tests do).
  - `errorTrackingBody` — a concrete named `io.ReadCloser` that buffers up to 8 KB of the body, and on `Close()` emits exactly one DEBUG record (via `sync.Once`), even on early close / read error.
  - `addOpenTelemetryTransport` now also fires on the `LOGGING` flag, wiring `Options.Logger` (with static telemetry attributes attached, mirroring gRPC) into the transport, while `otelhttp` still wraps the chain so a span is always created.
  - Log building (`logHTTPError`): `msg`, `rpc.system.name=http`, `rpc.response.status_code` (gRPC-style), `http.response.status_code` (numeric), `http.request.method`, `error.type`, plus optional `gcp.errors.domain`, `gcp.errors.metadata.<k>`, `http.request.resend_count`, `gcp.resource.destination.id`.
  - Body parsing picks the first `google.rpc.ErrorInfo` detail with a reason for `error.type`/`domain`/`metadata`; `ContentLength > 8192` logs immediately with the status string and does **not** wrap; content exceeding 8192 with unknown length falls back to the status string.
  - Transport errors: `DeadlineExceeded`→`CLIENT_TIMEOUT`/`DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, `Canceled`→`CLIENT_CANCELLED`/`CANCELED`, else `%T`/`UNKNOWN`.
- **`auth/httptransport/transport.go`** — removed the moved OTel code and pruned now-unused imports.
- `Options.Logger` already existed, so no change was needed there.

**Verification:** I wrote a throwaway test exercising every requirement (actionable reason, domain/metadata, resend/resource context, all three transport-error classes, both >8 KB fallbacks, early close, logging disabled, and the full `NewClient` feature-flag matrix for logging/tracing independence), confirmed all behaviors, then removed it. Existing tests pass, `-race` is clean, and the whole module builds.

One design note worth flagging: the "span still recording when the log is emitted on body close" guarantee holds when `otelAttributeTransport` is constructed directly with a caller-provided span (how `TestTelemetryTransport` builds it). Through the full `otelhttp` path it cannot hold for *any* implementation, because `otelhttp`'s wrapped body calls `span.End()` before delegating `Close()` to the inner body — so that requirement is inherently a direct-construction scenario, which my emit-on-`Close` design satisfies.
